featured_reviews.name: Review Man
featured_reviews.review_text:
Harley’s Ivory Lounge

We walked into Harley’s Ivory Lounge at Kala Ghoda with two things guiding us. The almost unbelievable 4.8 rating across thousands of reviews and the dreamy photographs online that promised a café from another world. The approach did little to prepare us, for the street outside was dim and unremarkable, almost post-apocalyptic in its neglect. And then suddenly the café appeared, glowing like a castle from a fairytale, standing proud in the middle of ruin. Inside, the spell continued. It was heavenly in its beauty, every corner carefully crafted. The only slip was the use of AI art in some frames, which felt more tacky than tasteful, but beyond that it was a space that held you. The booths were elegant, the plating was charming, and the staff carried the same grace, explaining the menu patiently when it seemed unfamiliar. It felt like a refuge, especially for those who wander Kala Ghoda late into the night, since the doors stay open till midnight.

The food began with the pistachio medovik, the Russian honey cake that arrived layered like a poem. The pistachio sang most in the top layer, while the cream in between was rich and perhaps too thick, and the lower bread base leaned towards crumbly. Yet it was still a dish of substance, one that lingered on the tongue. Alongside came a lemon macaron, delicate on the outside, but the filling inside leaned harder than perfection would demand. The attempt was admirable, the execution almost there. The choco medovik hot chocolate was an indulgence, large in portion, flecked with medovik pieces, sweet and satisfying but tilting into cloying by the end. Its texture was smooth but not as luxuriously thick as some of the best, and perhaps a smaller, denser version would balance price and pleasure better. The small cube of medovik served alongside was a thoughtful touch, though in the company of so many sweets it became a test of endurance.

In the end, Harley’s Ivory Lounge dazzled us. The ambience was extraordinary, the staff warm, the plating memorable. The food had its strengths and its stumbles, but wrapped within such a setting, the flaws softened. Looking back, perhaps the ambience is carrying much of the weight of that near perfect rating. Still, it remains a place to which one would happily return, if only to try its savoury secrets and sit once more in a castle that rises out of nowhere.

8/10

This holiday season, we headed to South Mumbai and discovered a pure vegetarian and Jain dessert Cafe that instantly feels like stepping into a European wonderland.

One sip of their 7-layer Choco Medovik hot chocolate, and you immediately notice the finesse and thought behind every detail.

From beautifully curated festive gifting hampers and gift sets to Russian Medovik cakes, indulgent cheesecakes, delicate French macarons, along with a comforting coffee and food menu featuring pizzas, croissant sandwiches, and more, there’s something here for every festive craving.

Adding to its legacy, the cafe has also won a Guinness World Record for creating the World’s Largest Medovik Cake.

Choosing favourites wasn’t easy, but the Pistachio Delights and Lotus Biscoff Medovik are absolute must-tries.

📍 Located in Fort, Kala Ghoda, just a one-minute walk from BSE Mumbai, this place is definitely a must-visit, especially during the festive season.

featured_reviews.name: Sachet
featured_reviews.review_text:
I rarely leave reviews, but what happened yesterday was absolutely unacceptable and I will not stay silent about it.

We bought a tub cake to celebrate a birthday. Instead, it was completely ruined when we found a fly inside the cake. A FLY. In food meant to be eaten and celebrated with.

But what makes this even more infuriating is that this was not some freak accident. When we visited the store, there were flies visibly buzzing around the very area where the cakes were on display. This is not a one-off incident.. this is a hygiene failure. The display area was clearly not maintained to any acceptable standard, and yet cakes were being sold to unsuspecting customers without a second thought.

This is a basic food safety issue. Flies are carriers of bacteria and disease.. which i ate. The fact that customers are being served food in these conditions is not just disgusting.. it is a health hazard. Had a child eaten that cake, or had this happened to someone less composed, the consequences could have been far worse.

I strongly urge the management to take immediate action not just a surface level cleanup, but a thorough review of hygiene protocols, food storage practices, and display standards. This is not acceptable for any food establishment, let alone one selling celebration cakes.

Shame on you for letting it get to this point. Do better.

This was a very disturbing experience with Theobroma (BKC, Mumbai).

I am strictly vegetarian and had specifically ordered eggless pastries – Eggless Rich Chocolate Pastry and Fresh Cream Pineapple Pastry via Swiggy. However, what was delivered to me clearly contained egg. I realized this only after taking a bite and noticing the smell and taste. For someone who does not consume eggs at all, this is extremely upsetting and unacceptable.

When I contacted customer support, they initially denied the mistake. Only after I told them I was willing to send the pastry for lab testing did they apologize and promise that someone would pick up the incorrect item, conduct a quality check, and deliver eggless pastries.

That promise was never fulfilled. No pickup, no replacement, no follow-up.

Serving egg products to someone who has specifically ordered eggless food is a serious lapse in quality control and respect for dietary/religious choices. What is even worse is the attempt to deny the issue and then make false promises.

I expect Theobroma to publicly address this lapse and explain how such a mistake happened.

featured_reviews.name: Sourajyoti
featured_reviews.review_text:
Yazdani Bakery is one of those places in Mumbai that feels frozen in time. Started in 1953, it has been run by the same family for generations and still carries the old Irani café charm. The bakery is located in an old heritage building near Fort and Colaba, and the moment you step inside, you feel like you’ve walked into a different era — with its wooden furniture, old photographs, and simple, no-nonsense setup.
Yazdani is best known for its brun maska (soft bun with butter) and Irani chai, which is probably the most popular order here. Their mawa cake is legendary — rich, soft and full of flavour — and often sells out quickly. Other favourites include khari biscuits, apple pie, plum cake, and freshly baked breads and cookies. Everything tastes homemade and fresh, which is what keeps people coming back.
The place is not fancy, and service is simple, but that’s part of its charm. You come here not for luxury, but for nostalgia, honest food, and a slice of old Bombay. If you want to experience Mumbai’s Irani café culture and enjoy some classic bakery items, Yazdani is a must-visit.

featured_reviews.name: Sakib Mulla
featured_reviews.review_text:
Yazdani Bakery Takeaway: A Taste of Nostalgia
Yazdani Bakery is more than just a place to grab a bite; it's a living monument to Mumbai’s Irani cafe heritage. Opting for a takeaway from this institution is a smart choice for those eager to savor its legendary bakes without the old-school dine-in experience (currently limited anyway).
The magic lies in the Brun Maska—a crusty, yet tender, bread generously slathered with creamy butter—and the dense, aromatic Mawa Cake. These staples are impeccably fresh, a testament to the bakery's commitment to quality ingredients and traditional wood-fire ovens. Don't overlook the Shrewsbury Biscuits or the flaky, savory Khari. Packaging is basic and efficient—perfectly functional for transport.
While the interior retains a charmingly worn, antique aesthetic, the focus here is the edible legacy. The staff can occasionally be brisk, but the efficiency ensures a quick transaction. A Yazdani takeaway isn't just buying baked goods; it's securing a comforting, consistent piece of culinary history to enjoy in your own space. It's an indispensable, buttery, sweet slice of Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: yana
featured_reviews.review_text:
​Mango Mochi:
Unfortunately, this was a complete miss for me. The overall taste execution just didn't hit the right notes, and I wouldn't opt for it again.
​Sakura Cooler:
This beverage has a very specific flavor profile that didn't quite work for my personal taste, but I can absolutely see the appeal for a different demographic. It has a surprisingly low sugar content and carries strong, earthy notes highly reminiscent of green tea. If your palate actively avoids overly sweet formulations, you will probably really enjoy this. For me, however, it was a pass.
​Custom Fruit Tea:
This was easily the best part of the order and the one I actually liked. I customized it with a Jasmine Tea base, Lychee syrup, and Passionfruit boba and jelly. The flavor formulation here worked wonderfully. While the lychee and passionfruit definitely provided a distinctly sweet profile, it was never cloying or aggressively sugary. The floral notes of the Jasmine tea base did an excellent job of cutting through the sugar, creating a balanced and refreshing beverage.
​The Verdict:
I would recommend skipping the mochi, and only order the Sakura Cooler if you prefer an unsweetened, tea-forward drink. However, their custom fruit teas are recommended.

featured_reviews.name: Kartikeya Pathak
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Taste of Turkey: Hurrem's Turkish Baklava Confectionery Review

Located on the first floor of Jio World Drive, near the Tommy Hilfiger showroom, Hurrem's Turkish Baklava Confectionery is a charming open kiosk that offers a taste of authentic Turkish delights. We recently visited this sweet spot and tried the Pistachio Knafeh and Baklava – here's what we thought!

Ambiance: 4/5
Hurrem's has a small, limited seating area, but it's cozy and inviting. The kiosk itself is beautifully decorated with traditional Turkish elements, adding to the overall ambiance.

Flavors: 4/5
We tried the Pistachio Knafeh, which was a delightful combination of crispy phyllo, creamy cheese, and crunchy pistachios. The flavors were subtle and well-balanced, with a perfect blend of sweetness and savory notes. The Baklava was equally impressive, with layers of flaky phyllo, crunchy nuts, and a hint of sweetness.

Pricing: 4/5
The prices at Hurrem's range from ₹350-₹700 per item, with the average cost per person being around ₹400-₹600. While the prices may be steep, the high-quality ingredients and authentic Turkish flavors make it worth the splurge.

Verdict
Hurrem's Turkish Baklava Confectionery is a must-visit for anyone looking to try authentic Turkish desserts in Mumbai. With its convenient location, cozy ambiance, and delicious flavors, Hurrem's is a great option for a sweet treat.

Rating: 4/5 stars

Price: ₹400-₹600 per person

Recommended for: Those looking to try authentic Turkish desserts, and willing to splurge a bit.

Will I return?
Yes, to try more of their delicious Turkish delights!

Special thanks to Shivam, Nidhi, and Tanmoy for the wonderful hospitality and an unforgettable experience.

featured_reviews.name: Deep Sett
featured_reviews.review_text:
TOTALLY AVOID WASTING RS 5000.

At the onset this is probably one of the most expensive Buffets you would be having in Mumbai, priced at over 4300 plus taxes for a Dinner on a Weekday for an adult. Add to that, even as a gold accor member you probably get 20-30 percent instead of the normal 50 percent for 2 people is taxing.

The spread is decent, the variety in principal is there, but in terms of the taste and the quality of food, it’s really one of the poorest of the five stars , even considering the Leela and Lalit brands in Mumbai whose lay is very modest compared to this.

At almost 5000 you expect
1. Your veg sushi not being dumped in the refrigerator for you to pick up, questioning when it was made !

2. No juice , cold drink or mocktails are part of this offering. An advise to the team, you’re charging 5000 offering a drink probably at times could feel better than half the items on the menu.

3. I have seen just one Langarwaali daal the last 4 times I have gone here, to be honest , a Dal Makhani is the norm, if not that a top of the line dal Tadka.

4. Some dishes are borderline tasteless and on the menu just to increase the offerings on paper / website
A. Sushi - cold, refrigerated, and tasted as if it was made with zero interest.
B. Pizza Margerita- looked like an Udipi version not one served at a top 5 star, see the pictures yourself.
C. Fattoush salad, I mean if anyone has had a look at what they serve with that name, it’s embarrassing.
D. Starters like paneer tikka seem like lying there unattended for hours.
E. Many of the deserts too seem just good looking and tasting on borderline just sugar toffees.

When you come to a place , the stature of a Sofitel From the ACCOR elite stable, you expect basic standards and taste but unfortunately that’s missing.

The fact that it’s in BKC and most people have very little options for a 5 Star experience, plus because of its location the occupancy is high, is the best answer to why it’s half full during these buffets otherwise as per the taste of the food it should be  probably amongst the slowest moving places ever.

Sofitel I have over 11 million people reading this, so I’m saying this with humility please pull up and improve , make prices more competitive and the food seem like it’s made with care for the guests and hopefully the most charm would be back.

Till then all the best!!

featured_reviews.name: Aiman Behlim
featured_reviews.review_text: Visited Theobroma Café in Borivali, and once again, it proved why it’s one of the best cafés in Mumbai! I tried the Chicken Makhani Sandwich and the Chicken Mayo 🥪 —both were absolutely loaded, bursting with flavor, and made with fresh, soft bread. Every bite was mouth-watering and satisfying, served with a tasty side of sauce that perfectly complemented the sandwiches. For dessert, I went for the Hazelnut pastry 🍰 and wow—just wow! The rich, exotic mousse simply melted in my mouth, with the fine taste of hazelnut shining through in every bite. It was pure indulgence—yum yum yummm! The café also offers fresh loaves of bread, chocolate spreads, and more. If you’re ever craving something delicious, whether savory or sweet, Theobroma is a must-visit!🎖️

featured_reviews.name: D.M Enterprises
featured_reviews.review_text: The staff doesnt even put topper in the delivery as promised in swiggy description - it was anniversary special cake with topper. This outlet sent me wrong design and no topper whole celebration got spoilt no accountability even after complaining. Never ordering again.

featured_reviews.name: Tejas Sawant
featured_reviews.review_text: Visited Theobroma, Borivali and tried the Hazelnut Praline pastry, Eggless Chocolate Rich pastry, and the Millionaire Brownie — all three were absolutely delicious! The flavors were rich, textures perfect, and each bite felt like a premium dessert experience. The service was smooth, and the staff was polite and attentive, which made the visit even more enjoyable. Highly recommended for anyone with a sweet tooth looking for quality desserts in Borivali!

featured_reviews.name: Ayyub Kolsawala
featured_reviews.review_text:
This doesnt need any introductions. After a heavy dinner at Maa Anjaani pav bhaji, we went straight for desserts at Theobroma.

Theobroma wasn’t always my go-to place but it has recently become one. Not only do they serve delicious brownies, their pastries are also pretty good.

Fresh Cream Pineapple Pastry ♥️🔥: A very simple yet delicious pastry. I absolutely love their cream and pineapple filling which makes a perfect combination. It’s not too sweet making it perfect for a post dinner dessert item. Must try even if you don’t enjoy fruit cakes, this will leave you craving for it.

Hazelnut Praline Mousse Cake ♥️: When I am craving a chocolate cake, this is the one I go for. Its delicious!

New York Style Cheesecake ♥️: It was delicious and definitely worth trying.

Sourdough Bread ♥️: Recently I purchased their sourdough bread for sandwiches and after lightly toasting the bread, I was very happy with it’s texture and flavour. They charge 120 for it which makes it extremely valuable for the money spent.
